description: Connect a mailbox by SMTP and IMAP. We sign in to both first. If either login fails, nothing is saved and it answers 400. `details` has one entry for each login that failed: `path` is the login (`smtp` or `imap`) and the field to fix (`host` or `password`), and `code` is the reason. For each `code`: `dns` (the host name was not found): check it with your provider. `refused` (the server refused the connection): check the port and that the service is turned on. `timeout` (the server did not answer in time): check the port and the security setting. `tls` (the secure connection or the server's certificate failed): use the host name your provider gives you, or ask them to fix the certificate. `starttls_missing` (the server does not offer STARTTLS, and we never sign in without encryption): ask your provider for its encrypted port. `auth` (the username or password was refused): check both, or use an app password if your provider needs one. `rate_limited` (the provider temporarily limits logins): wait a few minutes and try again without changing the password. `access_denied` (your provider says IMAP is off for this account): in Zoho Mail, open Settings, Mail Accounts, select your address and turn on IMAP Access, or ask your admin to allow it, then try again. `app_password_required` (Google needs an app password): turn on 2-Step Verification, create one, and use it as the password. `host_not_public` (the host is a private address): use your provider's public mail server. `microsoft_needs_graph` (Microsoft takes no password here): a signed-in owner uses start_microsoft_connect, and an API key asks for that with create_handoff (kind connect_mailbox). If the check can't finish in 15 seconds it answers 503 and saves nothing: try again. A working login does not prove that the address is yours: nothing sends from this mailbox until request_mailbox_confirmation and confirm_mailbox_address confirm it. Leave `handoffId` out with an API key: it is for the console, and a key that sends it gets 400. It needs setup permission. A signed-in owner has it and can give it to an API key for the whole workspace. That key loses it if its maker stops being the owner.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: connect_mailbox
title: Connect a mailbox
